title: Shallowest Leaf Depth
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree. Return the number of nodes on the shortest path from the root down to a leaf, counting both ends. For an empty tree, return 0.

A leaf is a node with no children at all. A node with only one child is not a leaf, so a path cannot stop there.

examples.why: The 3 is a leaf right below the root: two nodes on the path.
A chain leaning right. The root's missing left child is not a leaf, so the only leaf is the 3, three nodes down.
An empty tree has no path at all.

hints: The usual depth recursion takes the minimum of the two subtree depths. What goes wrong when one child is missing?
A missing child is not a leaf, so its depth of 0 must not win the minimum. If one side is empty, the answer must come from the other side.
Breadth-first search finds the answer without visiting the whole tree: walk level by level and stop at the first node with no children.

explain.intuition:
The trap is the one-child node. Copying the maximum-depth recursion and swapping max for min makes an empty side return 0 and win, so the chain [1, null, 2, null, 3] would report 1. A path has to end at a real leaf. When one child is missing, recurse only into the other.

Breadth-first search fits this question better. It visits the tree one level at a time, so the first leaf it meets is the shallowest one, and it can stop right there. On a lopsided tree, like a DOM with one huge deep branch and a shallow sibling, BFS skips most of the work.
steps: Put root in a queue with depth 1.
Pop nodes in order. If a node has no left and no right child, return its depth.
Otherwise push its existing children with depth + 1.
pitfalls: Using 1 + min(left, right) without handling a missing child. A missing child gives 0, which is not a leaf.
Returning 1 for an empty tree instead of 0.
Recursive DFS on a chain of 100 000 nodes can overflow the call stack. BFS uses a queue and avoids it.

solutions.title: Depth-first recursion
solutions.idea: If one child is missing, the answer comes from the other one. Only when both exist take the minimum.

solutions.title: Breadth-first, stop at the first leaf
solutions.idea: Visit level by level. The first node without children is on the shallowest level.

followups: Return the values on that shortest root-to-leaf path. If two leaves tie, which one does BFS give you?
Return the depth of the deepest leaf instead. Can BFS still stop early?
